When there are pending creates, `pulumi refresh` prompts you interactively: select "clear" if the resource was not created, or provide the resource's physical ID so Pulumi can import it if it was created. Confirm the status of the resources in your cloud provider console first. After this, your stack should be valid, up-to-date, and ready for future updates.

question: pulumi refresh non interactive import pending creates two flags
reference_answer:
Use `--import-pending-creates` to specify each resource, passing the resource URN and its physical ID as two consecutive flag invocations, one for the URN and one for the ID. Example:
```bash
pulumi refresh \
  --import-pending-creates "urn:pulumi:dev::myproject::aws:s3/bucket:Bucket::mybucket" \
  --import-pending-creates "my-bucket-abc123" \
  --yes
```
For multiple pending creates, alternate URN and physical ID invocations in order:
```bash
pulumi refresh \
  --import-pending-creates "urn:pulumi:dev::myproject::aws:s3/bucket:Bucket::bucket1" \
  --import-pending-creates "bucket1-id" \
  --import-pending-creates "urn:pulumi:dev::myproject::aws:s3/bucket:Bucket::bucket2" \
  --import-pending-creates "bucket2-id" \
  --yes
```
The URN can be found in the `pulumi up` diagnostic output or by running `pulumi stack --show-urns`. Combining URN and ID in a single invocation fails with `each URN must be followed by an ID: found an odd number of entries`, and passing both as arguments to one flag fails with `unknown command "my-id" for "pulumi refresh"`.

question: Can I clear all pending creates in CI without being prompted, if the resources never got created?
reference_answer: Yes. In CI/CD environments or scripts where interactive prompts aren't available, use the following command to clear all pending creates when the resource was not created: `pulumi refresh --clear-pending-creates --yes`

question: my readme button is showing as a broken image after I pasted it on github, what's wrong with the link
reference_answer: Use the fully qualified image URL rather than a relative path. A relative path only resolves on pulumi.com and renders as a broken image once the snippet is pasted into a README hosted elsewhere. The button image should be referenced with a full URL such as https://www.pulumi.com/images/deploy-with-pulumi/button.svg, as in the Markdown example: [![Deploy](https://www.pulumi.com/images/deploy-with-pulumi/button.svg)](https://app.pulumi.com/new?template=https://github.com/pulumi/examples/aws-ts-s3-folder)

question: button for my template pointing to a specific branch or tag, python pulumi
reference_answer: Use a fully qualified GitHub URL with the template parameter to reference the template at a specific Git branch, tag, or commit, for example: https://github.com/pulumi/examples/tree/master/aws-ts-s3-folder

question: Can I use the SVG or PNG for the deploy button, or does it need a dark mode version too?
reference_answer: The button works on light and dark backgrounds, so there is no theme variant to pick. Use either the SVG or the PNG: https://pulumi.com/images/deploy-with-pulumi/button.svg or https://pulumi.com/images/deploy-with-pulumi/button.png. The SVG is generally the better choice since it stays sharp on high-density displays. Older snippets pointing at light.svg, light.png, dark.svg, or dark.png still work and serve this same button.

question: so the operator just applies whatever version i point it at right away? there's no step where i can review it first?
reference_answer: By default the Pulumi Kubernetes Operator applies changes immediately. When the version a Stack tracks changes, the operator runs pulumi up and reconciles your infrastructure to it, with no built-in pause for review. The safety of a rollout therefore depends on approving a change before its version reaches the operator, and previewing it upstream where you need one. Once a change is approved, spec.prerequisites stages how it lands, holding each environment until the one before it succeeds.

question: k8s operator pulumi pinned commit preview before promote ci
reference_answer: When the Stack pins spec.commit, previewing before promotion works cleanly because the commit is immutable, so CI previews the exact version you later promote. Steps: 1. Open a pull request against the program repository; CI previews it. 2. Merge once the preview is green. 3. Advance spec.commit on the Stack to the merged SHA in a reviewed pull request against your manifests. The operator reconciles the new commit only after the manifest change merges, and that commit was already previewed. This is the recommended pattern for production and composes with prerequisites to order the environments the promoted commit lands in.

question: the prerequisite has succeededWithinDuration set to 1h, what happens if the last successful run was longer ago than that? does the dependent stack just wait forever?
reference_answer: The optional requirement.succeededWithinDuration sets a freshness window on the prerequisite: with 1h, its last successful run must have completed within the last hour. If it's older, the operator re-syncs the prerequisite and waits for it to succeed again before the dependent stack proceeds. The dependent stack does not wait indefinitely on a stale prerequisite; the operator re-runs the prerequisite and then waits for that new run to succeed.

question: Can I preview an inline Program with the operator before it actually applies, since there's no repo to run pulumi preview against in CI?
reference_answer: You can't run a faithful CI preview before promotion with an inline Program, because there is no program repository to check out and config comes from the Stack, so a standalone pulumi preview in CI has nothing to run against and no faithful way to reproduce the operator's inputs. You can still get a dry-run plan in the cluster by setting preview mode (spec.preview: true) on the Stack, which runs pulumi preview instead of applying. Set it back to false to deploy.

question: how do i call the pulumi cloud api from my terminal without writing my own http code, does it reuse my login?
reference_answer: Use the pulumi api CLI command. It inherits your existing CLI credentials, fills {orgName}, {projectName}, and {stackName} from the selected stack, and returns a stable JSON error envelope and exit codes that scripts and agents can rely on. Run `pulumi api list` to browse endpoints and `pulumi api describe <path-or-operation-id>` to inspect a specific operation.

question: curl pulumi api access token headers
reference_answer: Directly over HTTPS: pair an access token (see the access tokens concept page) with the standard Accept and Content-Type headers and call the endpoint with curl or any HTTP client.

question: so how do secrets get counted for my bill, is it every secret I write or only some of them
reference_answer: Secrets include static secrets (fn::secret), dynamic login credentials, and dynamic secrets. When using Pulumi ESC's document editor, each definition of fn::secret and fn::open::* (except with the pulumi-stacks provider) is counted as a secret. Only the secrets from the latest environment revision are counted towards your bill.

question: I'm trying to figure out if the secrets I put in an environment I edited last month still cost me money. Do older versions of an environment count toward the bill?
reference_answer: Only the secrets from the latest environment revision are counted towards your bill. Secrets include static secrets, dynamic login credentials, and dynamic secrets, and in the document editor each definition of fn::secret and fn::open::* (except with the pulumi-stacks provider) is counted as a secret.

question: where do I find the option to send my audit logs to an S3 bucket? I can't find it anywhere
reference_answer: Navigate to the organization's Settings, then Audit Logs. Use the three-dot menu and select "Configure Audit Logs to S3".

question: s3 audit log export IAM role external id steps
reference_answer: In the AWS console create an IAM role, select "Another AWS Account" and check "Require external ID". Provide the Account ID and External ID, then attach the policy you created (copied from Pulumi). Then provide the ARN of the IAM role, test the configuration, and after a successful test select "Save and Apply".

question: my azure foundry setup for neo, what do i put in the endpoint field and do i need the /v1/messages part?
reference_answer: In the Azure Foundry section, for the 'Azure resource or endpoint' field you can enter either your Foundry resource name, such as `my-resource`, or the endpoint's base URL, such as `https://my-resource.services.ai.azure.com/anthropic`. Do not include `/v1/messages` in the base URL. The API key goes in the Value field under Auth headers, where the header name is preset to `x-api-key`. Open the deployment's Details tab to get its key and endpoint.

question: Can I use my own Anthropic key with Neo and skip entering a model mapping?
reference_answer: Yes. Use an Anthropic API key scoped to the workspace Neo should use. Select Anthropic and enter your Anthropic API key in the Value field under Auth headers. The base URL and x-api-key header name are preset. Neo uses its configured Claude models through your Anthropic account, and you do not need to enter a model mapping. Your account must have access to the models Neo uses.

question: bring own model neo custom endpoint no fast model what happens
reference_answer: For Azure Foundry and custom endpoints, the default model is required. If you omit the fast model, Neo routes those requests to the default model too. The fast model is recommended and should be the model ID or alias your endpoint expects for a Claude Haiku model.

question: my deployment runs right away on every push and I need a human to sign off first, is there a built in approval step in deployments?
reference_answer: Deployments has no native approval gate; this workaround requires reviewer sign-off using an ESC Open approval. The linked Requiring Approval Before a Deployment Runs guide describes the workaround.

question: deployments downstream stack auto trigger when upstream changes, no loops or double runs?
reference_answer: The Dependent Stack Updates guide covers how to trigger downstream stacks automatically when an upstream stack changes, without duplicate fires or loops.

question: pulumi policy cli commands list create publish enable
reference_answer: The pulumi policy CLI commands let you create, publish, enable, and manage policy packs, policy groups, and policy issues from the command line. See the pulumi policy CLI commands reference at /docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_policy/.

question: Is there a list somewhere of the prebuilt compliance policy packs I can just turn on? I want to see which ones exist before writing my own.
reference_answer: Yes. The pre-built policy packs guide at /docs/discovery-governance/guides/pre-built-policy-packs/ covers the available compliance packs, with links to a reference page listing every policy in each one.

question: my ESC config needs a string but I have a list of numbers, how do I turn it into a string value?
reference_answer: Use the fn::toString built-in function. It encodes a value as its string representation. List values are encoded as a comma-separated list of the quoted string representations of their entries. For example, the list [1, 2] is encoded as "1","2". The declaration is: fn::toString: value-to-encode, where value-to-encode is any value to encode as a string.

question: esc fn toString mapping output quotes
reference_answer: Mapping values are encoded as a comma-separated list of "key"="value" pairs, sorted by key, where key and value are the quoted string representations of each key-value pair. For example, the mapping {b: y, a: x} is encoded as "a"="x","b"="y". Quoting is applied to each nested value, so entries that are themselves lists or mappings have their quotation marks escaped.

question: how do i get rid of a webhook on my stack, and can i skip the are you sure prompt?
reference_answer: Use the pulumi stack webhook remove command with the webhook ID: pulumi stack webhook remove <id>. It permanently removes the webhook from the stack and cannot be undone. You will be prompted to confirm unless you pass --yes, for example: pulumi stack webhook remove 1a2b3c4d --yes. It returns an error if the webhook does not exist. The -s/--stack flag selects a stack other than the current one.

question: remove stack webhook -y
reference_answer: pulumi stack webhook remove <id> [flags], with examples: pulumi stack webhook remove 1a2b3c4d (prompts for confirmation) and pulumi stack webhook remove 1a2b3c4d --yes (skips confirmation). The -s, --stack flag specifies the stack name and defaults to the current stack; -y, --yes skips confirmation prompts. The command is marked experimental.

question: i want to make a new project from one of our company templates but i don't want to copy the code into my own repo every time, can i just add a stack that points back at the template?
reference_answer: Yes. The New Project Wizard can add a no-code stack to an organization template without forking the template code. The template code remains the single source of truth, and the stack references the template directly. To do this, navigate to Platform → Templates → select a template → select Deploy with Pulumi (or Stacks → Create Project → select a template → Use this Template, which forks the code instead).

question: the wizard is asking me to authorize github and says it wants permissions for all my repos, why does it need that and does it use all of them?
reference_answer: For GitHub, the authorization requires permissions to manage public and private repositories and workflows. Pulumi uses these permissions to read template sources, write template content into repositories, and optionally create new repositories. While the authorization request includes additional repository permissions, Pulumi does not use all of them. This is due to GitHub lacking fine-grained repository permissions as part of the OAuth application scopes.

question: wizard config form not showing up for my stack, pulumi.yaml has no config section, what gives
reference_answer: Configuration value forms are displayed in two scenarios: when the project file (Pulumi.yaml) includes a config section directly, or when the project file references an upstream template via Pulumi.yaml (e.g., pulumi:template: https://github.com/org/repo/tree/HEAD/template-name). In the second scenario, the form uses the config section from the upstream template. So the form only appears if Pulumi.yaml has a config section directly or references an upstream template with pulumi:template.

question: my team wants pulumi to deploy stuff automatically when we push to git, and we already run kubernetes. is there an operator for that? how do i even start
reference_answer: Yes, the Pulumi Kubernetes Operator automates the deployment of Pulumi stacks from within Kubernetes. The Pulumi program for a stack can come from a Program resource, from a Git repository, or from a Flux source, and may be authored in any supported Pulumi language (TypeScript, Python, Go, .NET, Java, YAML). It provides custom resources to provision a workspace for a Pulumi project, keep a Pulumi stack up-to-date using gitops, write Pulumi YAML programs as Kubernetes objects, and run Pulumi deployment operations. To get started, follow the Installation section, which covers installing the operator, creating a service account, and configuring Pulumi Cloud access and Pulumi ESC, and then the Defining stacks section, which explains how to create a Stack resource from a Git repository, Flux source, or Program object.

question: pulumi kubernetes operator argo cd gitops
reference_answer: You can combine the operator with Argo CD to manage the lifecycle of your Stack resources using the GitOps paradigm, driving Pulumi deployments from the Argo CD UI or CLI. For comprehensive guidance, including a trunk-based GitOps workflow, preview environments, and sync waves, see the dedicated Argo CD with Pulumi Kubernetes Operator documentation at /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/argocd/.

question: my config value is a list and I need to set just one item inside it from the cli, how do I point to the right index?
reference_answer: Use a property path with bracket notation for the array index. Examples from the page include root.array[0], root.array[100], and root.array[0].nested. Property paths are used by the pulumi config set --path flag, so you can target an element of an array in a config object this way.

question: property path key has a dot in it
reference_answer: Keys containing special characters (i.e. [, ], ", or .) or beginning with a digit require bracket notation. For example, root["key with a ."] refers to a key containing a dot, and ["root key with \"escaped\" quotes"].nested shows escaped quotes in a key.

question: Can I use a wildcard to match every item in an array when I set ignoreChanges, or do I have to list each index separately?
reference_answer: Yes. A property path can use the wildcard [*] to match all array elements, for example root.array[*].field. The page also shows root.array["*"].field as an equivalent form. Property paths like these are supported by the ignoreChanges resource option, along with replaceOnChanges and hideDiffs.

question: my update failed halfway through, does pulumi just undo everything it already changed automatically?
reference_answer: No, Pulumi does not automatically roll back changes made during an update if an error or failure occurs. When an error or failure happens, Pulumi completes any pending operations currently in progress and then exits and reports the error. To accomplish a manual rollback after a failed deployment, revert the code and configuration changes of the failed deployment and run `pulumi up` to update your infrastructure to its previous state.

question: why doesnt pulumi check the real cloud state before running up or preview? seems like it would be safer
reference_answer: Pulumi does not automatically query your cloud provider's live state before running `pulumi up` or `pulumi preview`. Instead, it compares the desired state declared in your program against the last recorded state to determine what changes to make. This is an intentional design decision because refreshing requires a round-trip to your cloud provider for every resource in a stack, which adds significant latency, especially for large stacks. Pulumi's design treats your program as the source of truth for desired state, and changes made outside of Pulumi are treated as drift that you decide explicitly how to handle. To synchronize Pulumi's recorded state with the actual state of your cloud resources, run `pulumi refresh`. You can also refresh and apply your desired state in a single step using `pulumi up --refresh`. For automated drift detection and remediation on a schedule, Pulumi Cloud provides built-in drift detection.

question: pulumi config set secret encrypted in the yaml file?
reference_answer: Yes. When you set a configuration value, you may pass `--secret` to `pulumi config set`, which causes the value to be encrypted so it can be safely persisted in `Pulumi.<stack-name>.yaml`. Pulumi Cloud manages a unique encryption key for every stack, which it uses to encrypt that stack's secrets, and this can be configured to use your own custom secrets provider. Because a different key is used for each stack, the same value encrypted in two stacks will produce different encrypted strings, so you cannot copy an encrypted value from one file to another using a text editor. Instead, you must use `pulumi config set`.

question: it says experimental features are opt in, so are they safe to use in production if i turn them on?
reference_answer: No, you should not rely on them for production workflows. Experimental features are always opt-in and you enable them explicitly with a flag, command, or environment variable such as `PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL=true`. They are not necessarily supported, and they can change or be removed at any time without a deprecation cycle. When an experimental feature proves valuable, Pulumi invests in stabilizing it and promoting it to general availability, but until then its behavior can't be relied on.

question: so my team members on the Member role can run pulumi up on every stack if I set stack permissions to Write? does that also let them delete stacks with pulumi stack rm?
reference_answer: Setting Stack permissions to Write gives Member-role members the ability to view stacks and run updates on them, including `pulumi up` and `pulumi destroy`. However, removing a stack itself (`pulumi stack rm`) is not included. That requires the `stack:delete` scope, which is granted by the Stack Admin permission set and gated by the "Allow stack admins to delete stacks" toggle.

question: tag rule revoke access token stack creator grant
reference_answer: Tag-based rules only grant access. Like every other rule, they cannot revoke access that a principal already holds through another grant, so a tag rule is not a way to confine a principal to the resources that match it. A machine token that creates a stack holds a creator grant of Stack Admin on that stack and can keep operating on it even though the stack's tags do not match any rule in the token's role.

question: it says effective permissions are a union of roles, so if I give someone a custom role and they're already on the Member role, which one wins?
reference_answer: Effective permissions are the union of the user's organization role and all roles assigned to the teams they belong to. Each organization member has exactly one organization role (Admin, Member, Billing Manager, or a custom role), and team role assignments add on top of each member's baseline role. Members who have the Member organization role and have not been given an explicit custom role receive the baseline permissions defined in Organization-wide role settings. A member with an assigned custom role uses that role instead of those organization-wide settings.

question: How many custom roles can I create on the Pro edition, and is there a limit on Enterprise?
reference_answer: The Pro edition allows up to 25 custom roles, and the Enterprise edition allows unlimited custom roles.

question: my automation keeps running but i want it to not change anything in my infra, is it read only by default?
reference_answer: Yes. Scheduled tasks default to two settings. Approval mode is auto, so the task proceeds without waiting for human confirmation at each step. Permission mode is read-only, so the task can read state and propose changes through pull requests, but it can't write directly to your infrastructure. Settings apply in this order: the per-automation setting if set, then the org-level default, then auto approval and read-only permissions (the built-in fallback).

question: automation run permissions rbac which user
reference_answer: A scheduled task runs with the RBAC permissions of the user who scheduled it, evaluated at execution time. If that user's permissions change between scheduling and execution, the new permissions apply.

question: Can I set up an automation to run hourly, daily, or weekly, and what happens once I save it?
reference_answer: The form asks for a name, the prompt (which includes the same integration selector as an ad-hoc task), and the frequency (hourly, daily, weekdays, or weekly). Save the automation and it begins running at the next scheduled tick.

question: I want my deployments to pull my private image from Amazon ECR, so I pasted in my ECR password and it worked at first, but now deployments fail to pull the image. What am I doing wrong?
reference_answer: Private registries only support static username and password credentials, not OIDC or IAM-role-based pulls, so a private Amazon ECR registry does not work for custom executor images. ECR's registry password is an authorization token from `aws ecr get-login-password` that expires after 12 hours, so a pasted token soon stops working and deployments can no longer pull the image. A public image on Amazon ECR Public needs no credentials and works fine. If you need to pull a private ECR image, or your security model requires short-lived registry credentials, use customer-managed runners, which run in your own infrastructure and can authenticate to the registry with an IAM role or any other mechanism you configure.

question: executor root path non root user custom image permission denied
reference_answer: By default, the deployment executor uses `/` as its root path. If your image runs as a non-root user that can't write there, turn on **Customize the executor root path** and set **Executor root path** to a writable directory, such as `/tmp`. This toggle appears only when a custom executor image is in use, or when the stack already has a root path set.

question: how do I make a policy only warn instead of blocking the update, and can I change that without editing the code?
reference_answer: Set enforcementLevel to "advisory" in the policy (Python: enforcement_level=EnforcementLevel.ADVISORY) to warn only. Only enforcementLevel can be overridden without changing the policy pack's code. Set it in the policy pack's configuration, either for one policy or for every policy with the all key, for example: {"all": "advisory", "rds-storage-encrypted": "mandatory"}. All other fields, including severity, are fixed when you publish the pack.

question: python policy remediation_steps vs remediate enforcement?
reference_answer: They are unrelated. remediation_steps (remediationSteps in TypeScript) is guidance for fixing a violation by hand. The remediate enforcement level fixes resources automatically. Enforcement levels are advisory (warn only), mandatory (block the update), remediate (fix the resource automatically), or disabled (turn the policy off).

question: Its says severity is fixed at publish time, so how do I change a policy's severity later?
reference_answer: Severity is fixed when you publish the pack. To change it, update the code and publish a new version. Only enforcementLevel can be overridden through the policy pack's configuration without changing code.

question: In TypeScript do I have to fill in all four framework fields (name, version, reference, specification) or can I skip some, and what about Python?
reference_answer: In TypeScript, all four fields are required when you set framework: name, version, reference, and specification. In Python, PolicyComplianceFramework accepts each one as optional.

question: infisical secrets get config esc yaml example
reference_answer: Use the infisical-secrets provider under fn::open::infisical-secrets, passing the login output from the infisical-login provider and a get map. Each key in get is the name you want to reference, and its value specifies projectId, environment, and secretKey. Example: values: infisical: login: fn::open::infisical-login: oidc: identityId: aaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee; secrets: fn::open::infisical-secrets: login: ${infisical.login} get: api-key: projectId: xxxxxxx-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee environment: prod secretKey: api-key; app-secret: projectId: xxxxxxx-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee environment: dev secretKey: app-secret. You can then map the results into pulumiConfig, for example apiKey: ${infisical.secrets.api-key} and appSecret: ${infisical.secrets.app-secret}. The provider returns a map of names to secrets.

question: ok I set up the OIDC part like the guide said, how do I check it actually works from my end?
reference_answer: Validate the configuration by running the pulumi env open command of the Pulumi CLI, replacing <org>, <project>, and <environment> with your Pulumi organization name and environment identifier: pulumi env open <org>/<project>/<environment>. If the configuration is working, the output should look similar to a JSON object containing infisical.login.accessToken and infisical.secrets with the resolved values, for example api-key set to my-api-key and app-secret set to my-app-secret.

question: i want to turn off a webhook in my pulumi org without deleting it, what command do i run
reference_answer: Use the edit command with the --active flag set to false: pulumi org webhook edit <id> --active=false. For example: pulumi org webhook edit 1a2b3c4d --active=false. Only the flags you pass are changed; all other fields are preserved.

question: pulumi webhook add event remove event incrementally
reference_answer: Use --add-event and --remove-event (and --add-group and --remove-group) to modify event subscriptions incrementally. Example: pulumi org webhook edit 1a2b3c4d --add-event deployment_failed --remove-event deployment_started. Only the flags you pass are changed; all other fields are preserved.
